common_name: Aromi Lemonade Azalea (Fragrant Yellow Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter worked in; site in dappled shade to morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Bred by Dr. Eugene Aromi of Mobile, Alabama as part of his heat- and humidity-tolerant native azalea breeding line, Lemonade produces large, soft yellow flowers with a darker yellow blotch, carried in trusses of six to eight blooms per cluster in spring. It grows into a rounded, medium-sized deciduous shrub well suited to a woodland-edge border in Gulf South gardens. Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, acidic soil and avoid heavy pruning, since flower buds set on the previous year's growth.

common_name: Aromi Spring Sensation Azalea (Fragrant Pink Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in well-drained, acidic soil rich in organic matter, in dappled shade to morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Bred by Dr. Eugene Aromi from a cross of the Gulf South native Rhododendron canescens with an Exbury hybrid azalea selection, Spring Sensation carries large, fragrant, light pink flowers in full, rounded trusses in mid-to-late spring. It grows into a substantial, upright deciduous shrub reflecting the vigor of its native canescens parent, and shares that species' Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil at a woodland edge or high-canopy shrub border.

common_name: Aromi King's Wizard Azalea (Fragrant Bronze-Gold Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in average, rich, well-drained acidic soil in bright to mostly shade; water regularly during the first growing seasons.

directions: Part of Dr. Eugene Aromi's deciduous native azalea breeding line from Mobile, Alabama, King's Wizard bears large, rounded clusters of fragrant, golden-yellow flowers touched with bright red and marked with a darker orange blotch. Bloom opens in early spring just before or as the new foliage emerges, and the nectar-rich flowers draw butterflies and hummingbirds. It grows into a large, heat- and humidity-tolerant deciduous shrub well suited to a woodland-edge planting in Gulf South gardens; give it room to reach its substantial mature size.

common_name: Aromi Pat Ryan Azalea (Fragrant Peach-Orange Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled shade to morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Bred by Dr. Eugene Aromi in Mobile, Alabama as part of his heat-tolerant native deciduous azalea line, Pat Ryan opens fire-red buds into large, spicy-sweet-scented flowers with ruffled, multi-toned petals in shades of peach, pink, orange, and golden yellow with a yellow eye, borne in rounded clusters in early spring. The fragrant blooms draw hummingbirds and larger butterflies. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil at a woodland edge, where it shares the Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance typical of the Aromi breeding line.
